rendered: Not in general. The documents do not describe cobalt-free cathodes as having flat voltage profiles. The review on next-generation cobalt-free cathodes instead lists sloping voltage profiles as a drawback of disordered rock-salt (DRX) cobalt-free cathodes, attributed to cation disorder:[1][2] . Its figure of charge/discharge curves for common cobalt-free materials (NM82, NMT, NMM and NMA) also shows curves that slope across most of the voltage window rather than staying flat: Fig. 7[3]. For the NFA cobalt-free cathode, the study notes only that cell polarization was relatively lower in part of the voltage range ("[4]"), and it does not call the NFA voltage profile flat.
